summary: Task was to exercise the stock Toggle, Segmented, and Numeric controls via pointer/keyboard/clipboard/commit-cancel over the MCP drive harness, and leave a rendered frame. Both viable paths are closed over MCP, so I could not verify a single interaction outcome for the three target widgets nor render them. (1) The documented path — a WidgetPanel with a `children` list — requires each `WidgetChildSpec.config` to be pre-encoded wire bytes, and no MCP tool encodes structured child JSON into those bytes (widgets.md names this the missing 'generic nested-kind encoder'); the empty-children fallback stack is fixed to label/slider/radio/text_field/button and excludes all three targets. (2) The undocumented workaround — loading a widget standalone via `load_component export=aether.kit.widget.toggle` — works and is fully introspectable, but the widget is a black box over MCP: I drove pointer (aether.mouse_button+release), keyboard (aether.key Enter), and Collect directly into it and the handlers ran (visible as received/finished in send_mail_traced) but emitted nothing observable and logged nothing, because value-up events (ToggleChanged/SegmentedSelected/NumericChanged) and the Collect draw list both target ctx.parent(), which a top-level component lacks. As the closest achievable render artifact I loaded the reference WidgetPanel (built-in stack) into the live engine; it renders (label/slider/radio/textfield/button quad chrome, no glyphs since the font did not resolve), proving the compositor works — but it is NOT the target widgets. Engine 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 left alive.

artifact.rationale: The frame shows the panel with three abstract control widgets — a slider (blue-filled ~25% on a gray track), a stack of three checkbox squares (top one blue/checked, two gray/unchecked), and a large solid blue bar at the bottom — but no text or digits are rendered anywhere. The expected artifact requires the numeric editor to display "the committed validated value," yet no number is visible on any control; the bottom field that should be the numeric editor is a blank blue rectangle with no value glyphs. The committed validated value is therefore not shown, which is the concrete use-visible discrepancy.

papercut.what: The exact same PanelConfig JSON (with children:[]) was rejected when passed as inline `config` with 'config does not match aether.kit.widget.panel.config: field "$" expected object' (the Bytes $-embed resolver misfiring on the children Vec's element schema), yet loaded successfully via `config_path` pointing at a file with identical content. The two documented-equivalent input paths use divergent encoding, and the inline error is cryptic.
papercut.suggested: Route inline `config` and `config_path` through the same encoder; make the $-embed pre-scan skip empty/absent Bytes-bearing collections; and improve the error to name the offending field path instead of '$'.

papercut.where: input.md 'drive a component over MCP' guidance vs widget input model
papercut.what: input.md says to drive a component by mailing input kinds to aether.input, which fans out to subscribers. Widgets deliberately do NOT subscribe to aether.input (the panel root does), so that guidance silently does not reach a bare widget; input must be sent directly to the widget's own mailbox. Discoverable via describe_component's handler list, but a consumer following input.md would see no effect.
papercut.suggested: Note in input.md (or widgets.md) that stock widgets receive input by direct-to-mailbox forwarding from their root, not via aether.input subscription, so synthetic drive must target the widget/root mailbox directly.

missing-primitive.what: The only documented way to place a Toggle/Segmented/Numeric on a rendered panel is a WidgetPanel with a custom `children` list, but each WidgetChildSpec.config is a Bytes field holding pre-encoded child config. No MCP tool turns structured child JSON into those bytes (widgets.md itself calls out the absent 'generic nested-kind encoder'), and the empty-children fallback stack is hardcoded to label/slider/radio/text_field/button. A drive-medium consumer therefore has no way to render or host these three widgets at all.
missing-primitive.suggested: Add a nested-kind encoder at the MCP boundary that recursively schema-encodes structured child JSON into WidgetChildSpec.config bytes (using the child WidgetKind discriminant to pick the config kind); or ship a built-in demo panel variant whose fallback stack includes Toggle/Segmented/Numeric.

doc-gap.what: aether.key carries a numeric `code: U32`, but the docs only give the constant NAMES (KEY_ENTER, KEY_LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN, KEY_BACKSPACE, letters for Ctrl+A/C/X/V). To send a keystroke over MCP a consumer must read crate source (aether_kinds::keycode) to learn the values (e.g. Enter=0x0102, Left=0x0110, Space=0x0100, letters=ASCII). A pure docs+signatures consumer cannot press a key.
doc-gap.suggested: Publish the keycode name->value table in input.md (or a reference page), at least for the editing/navigation keys widgets match on.

blocker.what: A widget loaded standalone is unobservable. I sent aether.mouse_button press+release, aether.key (Enter=258), and aether.kit.widget.collect directly to the widget mailbox after config+frame+focus_gained; send_mail_traced shows the handlers receiving and finishing, but no ToggleChanged, no draw_list, and no actor_logs entries ever appear. Value-up events and the Collect WidgetDrawList both go to ctx.parent(), which does not exist for a top-level component, so nothing is emitted. There is no public way to observe or verify pointer/keyboard/clipboard/commit-cancel behavior of a bare widget.
blocker.suggested: Provide a minimal standalone widget-harness root (composites one widget and logs its value-up events, addressable over MCP), or have a parent-less widget mirror its value events into its own aether.log ring so actor_logs can surface them.
